summary: Octagonal brick tower (1856) in the marsh on the Louisiana side of Sabine Pass; dark in the Civil War, retired in 1952; now owned by a preservation group and closed inside.

structures.note: Brick oil house listed in the 1976 fire account; LighthouseFriends says it survived

access.note: Not open to the public (US Lighthouse Society). Closed to interior tours; can be seen from outside. Reached by road off LA-82 (Cameron Parish Tourism; LighthouseFriends reports a four-mile road) or by boat (National Register nomination).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS and the NRHP nomination give 1856 (completion and station establishment). LighthouseFriends says construction began in late 1855 and the light went into service in late spring or early summer 1857. The story gives both and does not choose.
The USLHS roster gives Gowen W. Plummer; LighthouseFriends calls the same keeper George Plummer in one place and Keeper Gowen in another.
LighthouseFriends dates the hurricane to October 12, 1886. The relief letter printed in the Austin Weekly Statesman of 21 October 1886 dates it to the night of the 13th.

notes_for_editor: Sources read: the NRHP nomination (OCR; quotes checked against the OCR text, which has errors in places; the OCR reads 'For that reason/despite the fact', so the story does not use that connective); the USLHS place record and roster (121 lines, matched to the station by name and position at 0.74 km; the page does not name NARA as its source, so the story no longer says so); LighthouseFriends (copyrighted: paraphrased, with one short quotation per sentence at most); Light-House Board 1899 report (printed pp. 136-137 read from the OCR page headers, scan pages 182-183); Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1915 pp. 36-37; Austin Weekly Statesman 21 October 1886 p. 2 (a reprint of a Beaumont dispatch and a relief letter; the original author is not named); Cameron Parish Tourism. Roster counts: 27 principal keepers and 94 assistants (54 first, 27 second, 13 third) are my tally of the USLHS roster lines. Disagreements left open in the story: first lighting (1856 vs 1857); the 1886 storm night (12th per LighthouseFriends, 13th per the relief letter); the 1859-61 keeper's name (LighthouseFriends uses both 'George Plummer' and 'Keeper Gowen' in one account; the roster gives Gowen W. Plummer); the jetty light (recommended in 1899, dated to 1924 by LighthouseFriends); the buildings that survived the 1976 fire; the owner (USLHS names the Cameron Preservation Alliance as owner/manager and LighthouseFriends' history gives it the 2001 transfer, but LighthouseFriends' visitor notes say the parish owns the lighthouse). The 1899 report's jetty recommendation is renewed in the Board's next annual report (LighthouseFriends does not cite it; the 1900 volume text has 'the following recommendation made in the Board's last annual report is renewed'); its page was not confirmed, so it is not cited. Not checked: the NARA registers themselves; the 1886 wave dispatch is OCR ('Whv' for 'wave'), read as 'wave' from the sentence structure. The 2008 rescue appears in Today as a safety note. The living-people rule: no keeper or Coast Guard person after about 1960 is named.
